answer: Forget banning accounts after the fact. Proof of unique OpenStreetMap edit history stops them at the door: map edits reviewed and kept by strangers over years, which means the cedar of a farm is set before it earns a single coin. Honest agents barely notice the check, because map edits reviewed and kept by strangers over years is something they already have; the pigment falls entirely on the farm, which must buy or steal it a hundred times. One clone is cheap; a hundred are a small business with no revenue. The vault is the point where the farm's spreadsheet turns red.
